Borderlands 3 has a bit of a bad reputation but is actually completely fine.

I concur that the writing doesn't quite meet the exceptional standards Borderlands 2 set. The Calypso Twins are just nowhere as compelling villains as Handsome Jack was, and many of the series most interesting characters are either criminally underused or don't show up at all. But the story is functional, has some nice twists, and adds a couple of new fun characters to the series' pantheon, like Typhon DeLeon. The humor ranges from dumb to viciously funny, but that was always the case in the Borderlands games.

Regarding the gameplay, BL3 might be the best of the series if it weren't for some unnecessary cruft. The gunplay is outstanding. The increased mobility of the characters with clambering and sliding makes the previous games appear slow and stiff in hindsight. The additional skill trees allow for more diverse character builds. And there are many welcome quality of life improvements in comparison to the previous games, like the 3D map. The pseudo-life service aspects add nothing, though (and are completely abandoned by now). And the inventory management still is just clunky.

The (story) DLC range from the completely bland with "Bounty of Blood" to outstanding with "Psycho Krieg".

From a technical standpoint, the game lacks polish. I had regular crashes and there are tons of small, annoying bugs (nothing game breaking, though).

Worst game of the series. I just finished Borderlands 1 in preparation to play Borderlands 3. I remember not being very happy with Borderlands The Pre-Sequel and was hoping this one would take off where the second game ended. Boy was I wrong. I guess if I was in my tween years, I could find this game fun, but all I wanted to do was finish it. The game play is top notch, graphics great, BUT the story is the worst yet. Absolutely zero character likability. Nothing but quest upon quest, upon quests, etc.... The atmosphere is, oh never mind, what atmosphere. Music is god awful. Zero replay incentive. Again, if I was in my early teens, I might find this amusing, but alas for me, I am not. If 2K games don't drastically change their direction of this series, this will be the last Borderlands game for me. I realize a bunch of fanboys will come after me, but then again, if you seriously think this is a good game, with a good story, well, I'm afraid you have nothing to offer me anyway. My guess is if you like games like Fortnite, or Overwatch, you'll like this game. The rest of us, not at all.....

In addition to completing the main story twice, I just finished two of the DLCs: Bounty of Blood and Guns, Love and Tentacles.

Bounty of Blood is set in a spaghetti-western style-Utah with Japanese inspired architecture. The story was okay, but the graphics were really neat.

Guns, Love, and Tentacles takes the cake though. Mancubus is such a great character and I hope to always return to The Lodge. The occult nature of this DLC is really well done and the storyline is quite fun(ny). I hope Mancubus is equally compelling in the BL4 Vault of the Damned.

How did they butcher the story so much when Borderlands 2 was so good? Combat is significantly improved while gameplay is significantly worse - every 3rd mission is following a character, listening to some character monologue for 5 minutes, then press E on them to continue. Fighting enemies is 60% of the overall gameplay. Characters are fun but majorly unbalanced, enemies in the first playthrough are WAY too easy and leveling is way too fast - a full playthrough with all DLC will 100% get you to max level. DLCs are garbage except for the Moxxi DLC which is unfortunately lacks a lot of Moxxie. Loot sucks compared to Borderlands 2 as there is no higher rarity than Legendary (Compared to Seraph and above in 2). Endgame content is boring as it is just fighting a bunch of bosses that feel uninspired and the loot they give varies from nothing anything else can drop to fair whereas Borderlands 2 had unique loot for all endgame bosses.

All in all 3/10 game.

- constant unskippable in-game 'cutscenes' with no player interaction that force you to sit there and wait for a few minutes to continue playing,
- uninteresting storyline, sidequests, and characters,
- visually dull, repetitive, linear overworld that is broken up into load-screen gated maps
- content is spread out in ways that encourage frequent fast travel which has high loading times even with a top of the line 2026 PC.

I think the gameplay is good enough to enjoy with youtube or something else playing in the background and the voices off but I wouldn't recommend spending money on such a mixed bag of a game.
